expected_evidence: geological: elevated concentrations of magnetic and carbon microspherules, nanodiamonds (lonsdaleite/cubic), platinum-group element (Pt/Ir) anomalies concentrated in a thin sedimentary layer at the Younger Dryas onset boundary (~12,900 cal BP / -10950) across multiple North American lake, loess, and peat sequences

material: 'black mat' organic-rich layer overlying the boundary, charcoal/soot spikes indicating continental-scale biomass burning, glass-like carbon spherules co-located with cultural (e.g., Clovis) horizons

astronomical/geochemical: cosmogenic isotope anomalies (e.g., Be-10, C-14 uptick), extraterrestrial helium-3 or platinum enrichment consistent with an airburst rather than a crater-forming impact (no crater expected given airburst mechanism)
genetic: megafaunal population bottleneck or extinction signatures and possible human (Clovis-era) population decline coincident with the boundary layer, though causally ambiguous

model_prior: existing scientific literature (Firestone et al. 2007 YDIH proposal and subsequent replication studies, meta-analyses, and rebuttals) documenting both supporting proxy discoveries and failures to replicate at some sites
response.rationale: This hypothesis aligns with the real-world Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (YDIH), which I recognize from training as a model-prior, not from evidence text provided here — flagged accordingly as low-tier/unverified within this pipeline. The proposed date (-10950, i.e., ~12,950 cal BP) sits essentially at the Younger Dryas onset, so I applied the 'younger-dryas' detectability row rather than a generic Paleolithic default, since sedimentary/geological preservation and dating control at this specific, well-studied boundary are comparatively strong (table values: geological 0.65, astronomical 0.7, material 0.35, genetic 0.3, model_prior 0.3). A cosmic-airburst mechanism (as opposed to a crater-forming impact) means the most decisive form of astronomical evidence — an impact crater — is not expected to exist even if the hypothesis is true, so absence of a crater is not informative either way; instead, evidence should manifest as geochemical/geological proxies (microspherules, nanodiamonds, Pt anomalies, black mat) distributed across many North American sedimentary basins, which are exactly the site types that survive well over ~13,000 years and that have, per model-prior recollection, actually been extensively sampled and debated (both supporting finds and failed replications reported in the literature). Because the relevant geological archive is widespread, datable, and has already been the subject of active search (unlike, say, textual or linguistic evidence, which are near-zero for this period), a genuine absence of confirming evidence at this stage would be somewhat informative against the hypothesis rather than simply a detectability artifact — hence I did not lower the adjustment further. However, genetic and material lines of evidence remain weaker/more ambiguous (extinction correlation vs. causation), and the overall episode remains genuinely contested in the scientific literature, so I set a moderate composite adjustment (0.58) — modestly above the raw geological/material average but below the higher astronomical proxy value, reflecting that some evidence types (crater, textual, linguistic) are structurally unavailable regardless of the hypothesis's truth, while others (geological/geochemical) are plausibly detectable and have plausibly already surfaced or been searched for, so a low-detectability excuse should not fully explain any absence of corroboration.
